title: Restore and validate audit chronology after KMS rewrap fanout failure
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: During a scheduled KMS rewrap operation on 2026-03-09 we observed a transient fanout failure in the rewrap controller which caused a subset of audit log shards to be written with an old envelope key identifier. Those entries were accepted by the ingest pipeline but were later rejected by the audit-indexer during ordering validation, resulting in a ~3 hour gap and timeline reordering for user-facing audit timelines in the compliance workspace. This ticket coordinates restoration of full audit chronology, validation of integrity across regions, and implementation of guardrails to prevent recurrence.

Scope: affects audit events for the interval 2026-03-09T02:10:00Z to 2026-03-09T05:25:00Z for accounts in us-east-1 and us-west-2 that were on the legacy rewrap path. Impacted surfaces: audit search results in Console (timeline missing entries, out-of-order events), downstream retention and export jobs, regulatory export bundles produced during window. No evidence of data loss at storage layer; primary issue is indexing/ordering and compliance traceability.
steps_taken:
1) 2026-03-09 05:30 UTC: Incident declared and emergency mitigation applied — temporarily paused ongoing rewrap fanout jobs and set controller to single-threaded safe mode.
2) 2026-03-09 06:10 UTC: Identified offending shards via ingest trace IDs and replays; created snapshot of raw audit blobs for the window to an isolated bucket.
3) 2026-03-10: Developed restore plan to reprocess raw blobs with corrected key metadata and replay through indexer with idempotent dedupe.
4) 2026-03-11: Ran dry-run reindex on staging; verified ordering correctness and checksum parity with unaffected periods.
5) 2026-03-12: Small production pilot reindex for two non-critical orgs; validated Console timelines and export bundles.
6) 2026-03-13: Rolled a coordinated reindex across affected shards, started at 03:00 UTC and progressing shard-by-shard with rate limiting.
7) 2026-03-14: Ongoing verification; now at ~70% completion of shard reindex and reconciliation.
findings:
1) Root cause: A race in the KMS rewrap fanout controller where concurrent rewrap confirmations could publish two different envelope key ids for near-simultaneous blob writes. When downstream indexer performed strict timeline validation it rejected entries whose envelope id did not match the expected epoch mapping, leading to those events being skipped from the audit timeline.
2) Secondary contributor: Our ingest pipeline accepted blobs with mismatched envelope id without tagging them for recovery; this allowed the data to be stored but not surfaced.
3) Observability gaps: No alert for 'indexer-reject-rate > 0 over 5m' existed; errors surfaced only in adhoc debug dashboards.
4) Customer impact: Several enterprise compliance exports for customers A/B were inconsistent with their raw export snapshots; legal/compliance teams flagged potential SLA breach.
5) No evidence of key compromise or exfiltration; KMS operations succeeded, the problem is metadata coordination during fanout.
